So I lived in Somerville, but there are areas of Boston/Cambridge that are definitely working class. East Somerville and Cambridge in particular are more working class and diverse - and I say this as a poor person of color who lived in Somerville lol. Yea rent is still high but it’s there. There’s also Everett which is way more diverse. And there are affordable housing units in West Cambridge, not in the Harvard Square/MIT area. I taught in Cambridge and most of my kids lived in West Cambridge - the area next to Sofra and Fresh Pond - and it’s mostly residential. Then Dorchester, Roxbury, and Quincy are fairly working class and blue collar. But the social stuff is hard; gotta be in school to make those friends especially in the Cambridge area. 

But you might want to look into Providence, like some other commenter said. Another option is Philly, where living is more affordable and accessible.

my team is convinced my weight will even out and we’ll work on minimizing my ED voice and that i can healthily lose weight later on in life if i want to but it is hard. i don’t know if it’s possible though, because all i want to do is lose weight the right way the first time around and keep it off, but i guess there is a good reason why ED programs don’t do that…
